source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Durham campus publishes 40 MW of IT capacity, the largest disclosed figure in North Carolina and 80 percent of all capacity the state's operators have made public.

North Carolina has 19 mapped data center facilities, but 14 publish no capacity information. The state's disclosed inventory therefore rests almost entirely on this single campus, which makes any statewide assessment of compute readiness unreliable.

At nominal densities, 40 MW implies roughly 400 racks at 100 kW each, or about 1,280 accelerators at 40 kW per GPU and 8 GPUs per rack. The operator publishes no breakdown by workload or tenant class, so this cannot be read as confirmed AI capacity.

The campus lists no certifications and no details on power infrastructure, PUE, grid operator, or power purchase agreements. Without those facts, the data cannot show whether the 40 MW can run continuously or at what utilization the local grid permits.
